issue.title: [number field] Preserve numeric precision while keeping default display formatting

labels.name: component: number field

issue.body:
- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

Fixes precision loss in the NumberField numeric pipeline while keeping the existing default display formatting. This is a compatibility-preserving fix: visible text still follows `Intl.NumberFormat` defaults (e.g. `1.235` for a no-format field), while the stored numeric value no longer loses precision when stepping or on blur.

## What was wrong

`removeFloatingPointErrors` rounded the stored numeric value to 3 fraction digits whenever `format` had no Intl rounding options. The 3-digit default was accidental: the original code intended a full-precision fallback (`... ?? defaultOptions.maximumFractionDigits ?? 20`), but `new Intl.NumberFormat().resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits` is `3`, so the `?? 20` never applied.

Consequences:

- `step` / `smallStep` finer than `0.001` were silent no-ops at the numeric level: incrementing from `0` by `0.0001` rounded back to `0`, so `onValueChange` never fired and the value never advanced. Native `<input type="number" step="0.0001">` works fine.
- Button increment/decrement always parsed the visible (rounded) input text before stepping, so a value like `1.23456` — displayed as `1.235` — advanced from the rounded `1.235`, dropping precision even when the input wasn't dirty.
- Blur re-parsed the rounded display text and committed it, so a focus/blur with no edits (or a blur after a programmatic change) collapsed the stored value to its displayed precision.

## What changed

**Numeric pipeline keeps precision (display unchanged)**

- Floating-point cleanup is now noise-only for no-format arithmetic. The no-rounding branch of `removeFloatingPointErrors` cleans binary noise (`0.1 + 0.2` → `0.3`) via `toPrecision(15)`, but only when the correction is within a capped epsilon (`min(Number.EPSILON * max(1, |value|), 1e-10)`). The cap stops `toPrecision(15)` from corrupting large fractional values and high-significance step values — e.g. `100000000000000.1 + 0.1`, `0.1234567890123456`, and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned verbatim because their delta exceeds the cap.
- Parsed input (typing, paste, blur) carries no arithmetic noise, so `toValidatedNumber` returns it verbatim when there is no step and no rounding format — keeping every typed digit, including values beyond 15 significant digits.
- This fixes `step` / `smallStep` finer than `0.001` at the numeric value level: the value now advances and `onValueChange` fires, even though the visible text still rounds per Intl defaults.

**Interactions read numeric state, not rounded display**

- Button increment/decrement: `useNumberFieldButton`'s `commitValue` now parses `inputValue` before stepping only when the input is dirty and uncommitted (`!allowInputSyncRef.current`). When the input is already synced, it steps from the numeric state instead of the rounded visible text.
- Keyboard `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`: same authority rule — parse `inputValue` only when the input has unsaved edits; otherwise step from the numeric state (`valueRef`). Previously the keyboard path always parsed the rounded display, so a synced field collapsed precision (e.g. `1.23456` → `2.235` instead of `2.23456`). Wheel and scrub already stepped from numeric state.
- Input blur: when the input wasn't manually edited and there are no rounding options, blur commits the stored numeric value as-is instead of re-parsing the rounded display text. A no-edit focus/blur, or a blur after a programmatic change, no longer discards precision. (With explicit rounding options, blur still rounds the committed value to the format.)

**Display formatting unchanged (compatibility-preserving)**

- The blur handler and controlled-value sync always format visible text with the default `formatNumber` path (the max-precision display path is removed). Visible text follows `Intl.NumberFormat` defaults exactly as before — no full-precision display by default.
- Explicit Intl rounding options from #4804 (`roundingMode`, significant digits, `roundingIncrement`, percent display-scale rounding on blur) are still respected; that branch is unchanged.

## Behavior (no `format`, value `1.23456`)

| Action | Displayed text | Numeric value (`onValueChange` / `onValueCommitted`) |
|---|---|---|
| type `1.23456`, then blur | `1.235` (Intl default) | `1.23456` |
| re-focus + blur with no edit | `1.235` (unchanged) | `1.23456` (unchanged, no commit) |
| increment `+1` (button or `ArrowUp`) | `2.235` (Intl default) | `2.23456` |
| `step={0.0001}` from `0` | `0` (Intl default) | advances `0.0001`, `0.0002`, … (was a silent no-op) |

Visible text matches the pre-regression default formatting; only the numeric value pipeline is corrected so precision is no longer lost.

## Tests

- Reframed the tests that asserted the accidental 3-digit numeric default or the max-precision display: they now assert default-formatted display text alongside full-precision numeric values.
- Added regression tests:
  - stepping from numeric state rather than rounded display text — buttons (uncontrolled `defaultValue`, and after typed precision is formatted on blur) and keyboard `ArrowUp` (synced `defaultValue`, and after a no-edit blur cycle);
  - a no-edit focus/blur cycle keeping full numeric precision, including subsequent stepping;
  - a canceled synced button step not committing a stale value after an external change;
  - sub-`0.001` `step` / `smallStep` advancing the numeric value and firing `onValueChange`;
  - `removeFloatingPointErrors` unit tests for noise cleanup (incl. negative), the capped epsilon (large fractional, high-significance step, safe-integer exactness), and verbatim parsed input beyond 15 significant digits.

- C1 is already fixed (the top-of-onKeyDown reset is gone as of f39fd5e8c). Worth noting: its suggested fix-direction ("fall back to parsedValue when parsedValue !== value") would actually re-break the core case — for a genuinely synced field, parsedValue is the rounded display (1.235) and value is full precision (1.23456), so falling back to parsedValue would reintroduce the precision collapse. The real fix was the dirty-flag ordering. I'll add the exact type → ArrowLeft → blur test to lock it in.

Fixed the others.

review_comments.body: `FLOATING_POINT_TOLERANCE` is used in two different ways: as a *relative* step epsilon in `snapToStep` (`stepSize * FLOATING_POINT_TOLERANCE`) and as an *absolute* cap in `removeFloatingPointErrors` (`Math.min(..., FLOATING_POINT_TOLERANCE)`). Coupling these makes future tuning risky: changing tolerance for cleanup would also change snapping behavior (and vice versa). Consider splitting into separate constants with names that reflect their units (e.g. `STEP_EPSILON_FACTOR` and `FLOATING_POINT_CLEANUP_ABS_TOLERANCE`).

The blur path can change the numeric value even when the user didn’t edit anything: after a prior blur normalizes the *display text* (e.g. to Intl’s default 3 fraction digits), a subsequent focus+blur will re-parse that rounded text and `shouldUpdateValue` will become true, causing `setValue`/`onValueCommitted` to round the stored value and lose precision. To preserve numeric precision by default, only update the value on blur when there was manual input (or a pending programmatic change), not purely because the formatted display text differs from the current numeric value.

This test comment is technically inaccurate: a “16 significant digit” decimal literal does not necessarily round-trip exactly in an IEEE-754 double (only certain decimals do). The intent here seems to be verifying that we don’t apply additional rounding/cleanup beyond JS number parsing, so the comment should reflect that to avoid misleading future readers.

`STEP_EPSILON_FACTOR` and `MAX_FLOATING_POINT_CLEANUP_DELTA` are currently the same literal (`1e-10`). Keeping two separate literals risks accidental divergence later and makes it harder to see that they’re intentionally aligned.

# PR #5040 Review — `[number field] Preserve numeric precision while keeping default display formatting`

**Author:** atomiks · **+623 / −97** · 9 files (4 source, 4 test, 1 util) · branch fetched locally as `pr-5040-review`

The core fix is **correct and well-motivated**: `removeFloatingPointErrors` no longer rounds the stored numeric value to an accidental 3-digit default, the step/keyboard/blur paths now read the authoritative numeric state instead of the rounded display, and the cancel/stale-commit guards check out. Tests assert both the numeric value *and* the display. No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md violations, no dead code, clean removal of `formatNumberMaxPrecision`/`getControlledInputValue`. The findings below are about edges and one regression.

> Verification note: agents couldn't run the Vitest suite (no `node_modules` in the worktree; the working tree has unrelated combobox changes). I verified the FP math in Node and traced control flow against `master` directly.

---

## 🔴 Critical (1)

### C1 — Typed value silently discarded on blur after a cursor key (regression, non-mirroring controlled `value`)
`packages/react/src/number-field/input/NumberFieldInput.tsx:181-194` (new `committed = value` branch)

The new blur branch `if (!hadManualInput && !hasRoundingOptions) committed = value;` trusts the numeric `value` over the visible text. But **any** key in `NAVIGATE_KEYS` (ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, End, Tab, Backspace, Delete) resets `allowInputSyncRef.current = true` at the top of `onKeyDown` and returns early — so a dirty input becomes `hadManualInput === false` on the next blur.

Verified trace (controlled field whose parent does **not** mirror `onValueChange` back into `value`, e.g. lagging/async/validated state):
1. Type `5` → `onValueChange(5)` fires, parent keeps `value = 0`, display shows `"5"`, `allowInputSyncRef = false`.
2. Press **ArrowLeft** (move cursor) → `allowInputSyncRef = true`, early return. Display still `"5"`.
3. Blur → `hadManualInput = false` → `committed = value = 0` → `shouldUpdateValue = (0 !== 0) = false` → `setValue` never called, no `onValueChange`; display reverts to `"0"`. **The typed `5` is silently lost.**

In `master`, blur set `committed = parsedValue` (`5`), so the value survived. This is a **regression**, reachable through the ordinary "type → arrow → click away" interaction — and the lagging-controlled pattern is one this very PR endorses with its new test `steps keyboard from dirty input text when the controlled value lags onValueChange`.

Note: the code-reviewer agent argued this branch was safe ("matches master because `parsedValue === value`"); that assumption doesn't hold here (`parsedValue 5 !== value 0`), which is why the deeper data-flow pass caught it.

**Fix direction:** only short-circuit to `value` when the text genuinely is the formatted form of `value` (e.g. fall back to `parsedValue` when `parsedValue !== value`), and add a "type → ArrowLeft → blur" regression test on a non-mirroring controlled field. *(Precondition is non-mirroring controlled; if the team considers that out of scope, downgrade — but it's silent data loss in a documented-supported pattern.)*

---

## 🟠 Important (3)

### I1 — `removeFloatingPointErrors` comment example is factually wrong + threshold imprecise
`packages/react/src/number-field/utils/validate.ts:45-47`

Verified in Node: `1000000.1 + 0.1 === 1000000.2` **exactly** (cleanupDelta = 0) — it is returned already-clean, so it does *not* demonstrate "noise left uncleaned." A genuinely-uncleaned example is `1000000.1 + 0.2` → `1000000.2999999999`. Also, the "above ~1e6" threshold is ~2× too high: a single ULP first exceeds the `1e-10` cap at the `2^19 ≈ 5.2e5` binade (`524288.3 + 0.3` is left uncleaned; `524287.6` is still clean). Suggest: fix the example to `1000000.1 + 0.2` and state "~5e5 (the `2^19` binade)".

### I2 — Large-magnitude binary noise leaks into `onValueChange`/`onValueCommitted`/form value
`packages/react/src/number-field/utils/validate.ts:51`

The documented tradeoff isn't contained to internal math: above ~5.2e5 the raw noisy value flows to the change/commit callbacks and the hidden form input, while the default-formatted display (`maximumFractionDigits: 3`) hides it. Verified: stepping `1000000` by `0.1` thrice yields `1000000.2999999999` to consumers while the UI shows `1,000,000.3`. Consider a magnitude-relative tolerance (compare significant digits rather than an absolute `1e-10` cap) so cleanup is consistent across magnitudes, or document the limit in public docs (not just a code comment) since it changes the numeric contract for large values.

### I3 — Asymmetric test coverage: decrement / ArrowDown from synced numeric state
`NumberFieldDecrement.test.tsx`, `NumberFieldInput.test.tsx`

The keyboard handler merged ArrowUp/ArrowDown into one branch and `useNumberFieldButton` rewrote both directions, but the new precision tests are almost all **ArrowUp / increment**. There's no test that ArrowDown advances the full-precision numeric value (`1.23456` → `0.23456`, not `0.235`), and the decrement button got none of the four precision tests its increment sibling did. A sign/direction-specific regression would pass the entire added suite (only the cancel case is covered symmetrically). Also: the >5e5 "noise left uncleaned" tradeoff is asserted only in a comment — add a unit test pinning `removeFloatingPointErrors(1000000.1 + 0.2)` returns the raw sum.

---

## 🟡 Suggestions (4)

- **S1 — Dedup the step+commit sequence into a context helper.** `NumberFieldInput.tsx:385-405` and `useNumberFieldButton.ts:55-65,114-133` repeat "refresh `lastChangedValueRef` on synced path → snapshot `prev` → `incrementValue` → commit if `committed !== prev`." AGENTS.md prefers sharing via the parent/context. A `stepValue(amount, {direction, currentValue, refreshCommitRef, ...})` on the root context collapses both. Keep `commitValue`/`currentValue` derivation and the `Home`/`End` unconditional-commit path *outside* it. (Verify against the cancel-after-external-change tests — commit-ref timing is delicate.)
- **S2 — `-0` flattened to `+0`.** `validate.ts:43` `parseFloat((-0).toPrecision(15))` returns `+0`; `Number.isFinite(-0)` doesn't guard it. Low reachability (the new early-return skips cleanup for parsed input), but a one-line `if (Object.is(value, -0)) return value;` is cheap correctness.
- **S3 — `toValidatedNumber` early return is broader than its comment.** `validate.ts:131-137`: the guard is purely "not stepping," so externally-supplied noisy controlled values (`value={0.1+0.2}`) are also returned verbatim, and the `Number.isFinite` guard is now path-dependent (only `removeFloatingPointErrors` enforces it). Broaden the comment to "non-stepping values (typed/pasted/blurred, and external)"; confirm `parseNumber` can't yield non-finite on the `clamp:false` path.
- **S4 — Clarity nits.** Reorder the blur `committed` if/else to lead with the dominant `hasRoundingOptions` axis (`NumberFieldInput.tsx:181-194`); add a one-liner noting `MAX_FLOATING_POINT_CLEANUP_DELTA` is an *absolute* cap vs the coincidentally-equal *relative* `STEP_EPSILON_FACTOR` (`validate.ts:5-6`) so a future reader doesn't merge them.

---

## ✅ Strengths
- Root cause correctly identified (the `?? 20` that never applied because Intl's resolved default is `3`); fix preserves display compatibility while restoring numeric precision.
- Cancel/stale-commit guards verified correct on the synced path: `setValue` returns before writing `lastChangedValueRef` on cancel, so the refreshed ref equals `prev` and no stale commit fires — and this is tested across all three entry points.
- Tests assert numeric truth (`onValueChange`/`onValueCommitted`) **and** display (`toHaveValue`), not refs. No `flushMicrotasks`-after-render or JSDOM-layout violations.
- Clean removal of `formatNumberMaxPrecision`/`getControlledInputValue` with no dangling references; imports correctly pruned.
- Excellent "why" comments with cross-path invariant references (the one factual slip is I1).

---

## Recommended action
1. **Resolve C1** (or consciously scope it out) — the only behavior regression; add the type→arrow→blur test.
2. **Fix the I1 comment** (wrong example + threshold) — quick and verifiably incorrect today.
3. **Decide on I2** — relative tolerance vs. public-docs the large-value limit.
4. **Close I3 test gaps** — symmetric ArrowDown/decrement precision tests + the >5e5 unit test.
5. Suggestions S1–S4 at the author's discretion.
